correctness.rationale: The integral formula follows from Lagrange inversion for U=1+zU^p. For an off-diagonal pair p!=r and every prime ell>max(p,r), Lucas gives binom(p ell+r,ell)=p mod ell, while p ell+r is invertible mod ell; hence R(ell)-R(1)=p-r mod ell, contradicting Dold divisibility for any fixed multiplier. On the diagonal p=r=s>=2, a_n=binom(s(n+1),n)/(n+1), and for odd ell>2s Lucas gives a_ell=s and a_(2ell)=s(2s-1) modulo ell. The Möbius sum at 2ell is s(s-1)/2 mod ell, a fixed nonzero residue, again impossible for a fixed multiplier. At (1,1), the constant-one sequence is realized by a singleton. Denominators used modulo ell are explicitly invertible. The finite verifier is only a spot-check of these formulas; the proof is unrestricted.
